species.name: Causal mechanism from provision to consequence
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces a credible chain from the proposed provision through behavior or implementation to a safety, health, environmental, or administrative consequence; score 0 when it merely asserts that harm or benefit will occur.
species.rationale: R10, R48, and R52 explain mechanisms linking regulatory choices to mining safety, noise exposure, or species survival.
all_names: States the causal mechanism linking the rule to its effect
Causal mechanism from provision to consequence

species.name: Independent/original evidentiary support
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment supplies verifiable data, measurements, test results, or independently gathered facts, as opposed to merely restating the notice or citing existing law/regulation text. A 10 presents original quantitative or empirical evidence gathered specifically to support the claim. A 0 offers no independent evidence at all -- only assertions, restated law, or unquantified characterizations.
species.rationale: R32 (Toyota) supplies original pull-force test measurements (26.9N, 114.4N, 306.8N) directly answering the agency's technical question, and R59 (tart citrus assessment) walks through an explicit expenditure calculation -- both dense_high_card_low. By contrast R43 (Iowa DOJ) proposes a specific $500,000 threshold with no supporting data on report volumes at that level, and R05 (NASACT) lists administrative burdens without quantifying any of them -- both dense_low_card_high, suggesting the scorecard rewards the topic of 'burden/threshold' without requiring it be evidenced.

species.name: Identifies a specific factual/technical inconsistency in the proposal
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment names and explains a concrete inconsistency, error, or gap between the proposed rule/notice and outside facts, cited service documents, or the agency's own stated rationale. A 10 identifies the exact inconsistency and its practical consequence for the rule. A 0 identifies no inconsistency and simply accepts or restates the notice's framing.
species.rationale: R40 (Orbital ATK) shows the NPRM misattributes root cause -- its own root-cause analysis found the LPT blade failure, not the bearing failure, was primary, which changes the appropriate compliance basis -- and R55 (Meggitt buckle SB) shows the proposed AD treats exactly 0.125 inch as unacceptable while the cited Service Bulletin lists it as acceptable. Both are concrete, checkable inconsistencies that a careful analyst would flag as substantive engagement with the rule's actual text.
all_names: Identifies a specific factual/technical inconsistency in the proposal

species.name: Engages and rebuts the strongest counterargument
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment explicitly names the strongest argument or justification for the opposite position and directly rebuts it point by point. A 10 identifies the specific counter-rationale (legal, technical, or policy) and dismantles it with reasoning. A 0 states a position with no acknowledgment that any opposing view or justification exists.
species.rationale: R48 (mine training) explicitly names and rebuts the Appointments Clause/APA argument for stripping District Manager authority, explaining why the authority is administrative rather than 'significant regulatory power.' By contrast, purely supportive comments like R21 (coral habitat) and R51 (shrimp moratorium) -- both dense_high_card_low or dense_low_card_high respectively -- state a position with zero engagement with any counterview, showing this dimension is independent of which model favors the comment and worth scoring on its own.
all_names: Engages and rebuts the strongest counterargument

species.name: Quantified, decision-relevant impact analysis
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment translates its concern or support into concrete, checkable numbers (dollars, rates, timeframes, population counts) tied to the specific decision at hand. A 10 gives an itemized, traceable numeric analysis relevant to the exact provision at issue. A 0 characterizes impact only in general, unquantified terms.
species.rationale: R59 (tart citrus) walks through last year's expenditures minus the removed fruit-fly-program cost to justify a specific new rate, and R33 (Medicare Part B teachers) grounds its request in concrete figures -- 35,000 retirees, a plan running since 2007, a 17-year cost-containment role. Both dense_high_card_low. By contrast R04 ('not enough effort') and R45 ('must be protected... for the greater good') give no figures tied to the actual decision at all.

species.name: First-hand expertise applied to the rule's specific mechanics
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the commenter's demonstrated personal/professional experience is used to make a concrete, technically specific judgment about how the rule actually works, rather than merely being asserted as a credential. A 10 shows expertise driving a specific operational judgment call (e.g., a precise recommendation grounded in lived technical detail). A 0 states credentials or affiliation but never connects them to any specific judgment about the rule's mechanics.
species.rationale: R19 (Black Sea Bass) uses 30 years of charter fishing plus a marine biology degree to argue specifically for bag limits over minimum size limits, explaining hooking and swim-bladder mortality in released fish; R39 (flight training) directly compares Part 141 vs. 142 performance standards from the commenter's own training and instruction experience. Both dense_high_card_low, showing dense may track expertise-in-use rather than expertise-as-signature.
all_names: First-hand expertise applied to the rule's specific mechanics

species.name: Traces downstream/second-order consequences
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment reasons at least one causal step beyond the rule's immediate, stated effect -- e.g., how an initial effect cascades onto third parties, markets, or future behavior. A 10 traces a multi-step cascade explicitly. A 0 addresses only the rule's most immediate, obvious effect with no further-order reasoning.
species.rationale: R20 (hot air balloon medical certification) traces a cascade from mandatory 2nd-class medicals to a shortage of certifying doctors to a training bottleneck to industry contraction, proposing a phased alternative; R48 (mine training) traces removed local authority to rigid uniform training to lagging behind hazards to elevated injury/fatality risk. By contrast R38 (VMS monitoring) raises pointed objections without tracing any further consequence.

species.name: Independent analysis beyond restating the notice or statute
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much the comment adds independent synthesis, critique, or judgment beyond paraphrasing the NPRM's own language or quoting the statute back at the agency. A 10 shows substantial independent cross-examination of the proposal's premises. A 0 is primarily a restatement of the rule's own summary or statutory language followed by a bare statement of agreement/disagreement.
species.rationale: R42 (NOSB organic standards) independently cross-examines the celery-powder nitrate loophole against OFPA's own prohibition and contrasts US methionine policy with the EU's welfare-linked alternative -- clear independent synthesis (dense_high_card_low). By contrast R11 (MFA) largely restates the proposed regulation's stated intent in near-identical language before declaring agreement (dense_low_card_high).
all_names: Independent analysis beyond restating the notice or statute

species.name: Concrete, checkable stakes vs. generic sentiment
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment describes who is actually affected and how, in specific, checkable terms (a named program, population count, operational detail), rather than invoking a general value ('protect the environment,' 'support small business') with no particulars. A 10 gives specific, verifiable stakes tied to the rule's actual mechanics. A 0 offers only generic value language with no particulars.
species.rationale: R46 (LA County DHS) cites 600,000 unique patients/year across four hospitals including two Level One trauma centers, tied to a specific payment-methodology provision; R33 cites 35,000 retired teachers on a named plan since 2007. Both dense_high_card_low. By contrast R45 ('must be protected... for the greater good... not just a few') states a value with no specifics of who, what, or how.
all_names: Concrete, checkable stakes vs. generic sentiment

species.name: Load-bearing precise use of technical terminology
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment's technical/domain language is load-bearing for the argument -- i.e., removing the precise term or figure would remove the argument's force -- versus decorative technical-sounding language that doesn't actually change or support the specific claim. A 10 turns on an exact technical distinction that is the entire substance of the objection. A 0 uses jargon or technical references that could be deleted without weakening the argument.
species.rationale: R55 (Meggitt buckle) turns entirely on the boundary condition 'equal to 0.125 inch' vs. 'greater than 0.125 inch' -- the precise number is the whole objection; R47 (International Aero Engines) turns on precise engine-model nomenclature (which models had suspect bearings installed) to justify narrowing the applicability list. In both, the technical precision is not decorative -- it IS the argument.
all_names: Load-bearing precise use of technical terminology

species.name: Explicit evidence-to-requested-remedy linkage
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment draws an explicit, traceable line from the evidence or reasoning it presents to the exact provision, number, or action it asks the agency to change. A 10 shows the requested remedy derived transparently, step by step, from the stated evidence. A 0 presents evidence/complaint and a specific ask as disconnected pieces, with no traceable link between them.
species.rationale: R59 derives its requested $0.02 rate step by step from the stated expenditure figures -- a fully traceable link from evidence to ask (dense_high_card_low). By contrast R23 (FDA youth tobacco survey) raises scattered methodological/privacy objections but its ultimate demand ('just a waste of government funding' since 2009) is never connected point-by-point back to the specific data-collection provisions it complains about (dense_high_card_low as well, showing this dimension can explain within-bucket variance too).

species.name: Acknowledges limits of own evidence or expertise
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment explicitly flags uncertainty, gaps in its own knowledge, or the provisional nature of a claim, rather than presenting all assertions with uniform, unqualified confidence. A 10 gives specific, honest hedging tied to a real gap in the commenter's evidence. A 0 makes sweeping, unqualified claims with total confidence despite no stated basis for that certainty.
species.rationale: R09 (supersonic aircraft noise) explicitly hedges: 'I can't say for sure, because I have little data to work with,' while still making its case (dense_low_card_high, showing this quality can go unrewarded by the scorecard). By contrast R34 (Scarlet Macaw) flatly asserts the listing 'is not going to help the wild population' with no acknowledged uncertainty about the underlying conservation science (dense_high_card_low), showing this dimension cuts across both buckets rather than tracking either model directly.
all_names: Acknowledges limits of own evidence or expertise

species.name: Comparative/analogical grounding in a real precedent
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment supports its position by pointing to a specific, verifiable precedent, prior case, or parallel jurisdiction/standard -- not a vague appeal to 'other places do it differently.' A 10 names a specific, checkable comparator and explains the relevant difference it implies for this rule. A 0 offers no comparative grounding at all.
species.rationale: R42 (NOSB) names the EU's specific poultry-welfare standard (slower-growing breeds, more space per bird) as the real alternative to synthetic methionine, and R03 (Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon) cites Castillo v. City of Las Vegas, 195 P.3d 870, as precedent for compensating sentimental-value losses -- both concrete, checkable comparators that ground the requested change.
all_names: Comparative/analogical grounding in a real precedent

species.name: Internal consistency between premises and requested remedy
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment's concrete ask actually follows from, and does not exceed or contradict, its own stated premises and evidence. A 10 shows every argument building toward a single, matched conclusion with no scope drift. A 0 shows the final ask is broader than, unrelated to, or in tension with the specific reasoning that preceded it.
species.rationale: R48 (mine training) keeps its legal rebuttal, safety rationale, and specific proposal mutually reinforcing throughout -- premises and ask match exactly. By contrast R23 (FDA youth tobacco survey) argues specific methodological/consent objections but concludes with a much broader claim ('just a waste of government funding' since 2009) that exceeds what the preceding argument actually established -- a scope mismatch between evidence and remedy.
all_names: Internal consistency between premises and requested remedy

species.name: Substantive novelty beyond the proposal's own preamble
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment supplies information, an argument, or a consideration that is not already contained in or obvious from the proposed rule's own preamble/summary -- i.e., whether it tells the agency something it did not already say. A 10 introduces genuinely new information or a new line of analysis. A 0 substantially restates the notice's own description of the proposal and states a position with nothing added.
species.rationale: R32 (Toyota) supplies original pull-force test data that resolves a technical question the notice itself left open, and R26 (Black-capped Petrel Working Group) brings field-level population, genetic, and habitat information from working scientists that goes beyond the agency's own Species Status Assessment framing. Both dense_high_card_low. By contrast R11 (MFA) restates the section's own stated intent in near-identical language before agreeing -- adding nothing the agency did not already know.
all_names: Substantive novelty beyond the proposal's own preamble

species.name: First-hand practitioner evidence from inside the regulated activity
species.instruction: Score how much of the comment's substance rests on knowledge the commenter could only have obtained by personally performing, operating, or living under the regulated activity. 10 = the comment reports specific things the commenter did, tested, measured, or repeatedly observed in that activity (a procedure run, a force measured, a condition encountered, how a practice actually plays out at the site), stated concretely enough that another practitioner could recognize or dispute them, and the recommendation turns on that experience. 5 = experience is claimed and lightly illustrated, but every substantive point could have been written without it. 0 = no experiential basis at all; the comment argues only from general knowledge, from the notice itself, or from an institutional position. Do not credit mere assertions of years of service or credentials; credit only transmitted observations.
species.rationale: R07 does not argue about the label at all -- it runs twist-and-pull, straight-pull, and single-stitch-pull tests, reports peak forces (26.9N, 114.4N, 306.8N), and compares the torn samples to labels recovered from the plant; that is evidence generated by the party in the best position to generate it. R14 is worth reading precisely because the writer trained under Part 142 and now instructs under Part 141, so the equivalence claim is a direct comparison rather than an inference. R56 supplies release-mortality experience from 30 years of fishing the actual stock at the actual depths. Against these, R38 and R40 take positions with no experiential basis whatsoever. A scorecard keyed to how a comment presents itself will over-read R38's polish and under-read R07 and R56.
all_names: First-hand practitioner evidence from inside the regulated activity

species.name: Audits the agency's own figures, record, or arithmetic
species.instruction: Score whether the comment tests the agency's stated justification against numbers or statements the agency itself placed in the record. 10 = the comment reworks the agency's arithmetic, or juxtaposes the proposal with the agency's own admission or its own prior rule, and shows the figures so the check is reproducible. 5 = the comment disputes a number but supplies no computation or source. 0 = the agency's figures are accepted or ignored entirely; the comment engages only at the level of preference.
species.rationale: R18 rebuilds the assessment-rate case line by line: the fruit-fly program is gone, so subtract $595,000 from last year's $751,148, compare against the $152,920 of proposed expenditures and the $282,572 reserve, and the reduced rate is shown to be affordable. R54 quotes EPA's own statement that it does not anticipate any HAP emission reductions from removing the exemption, then sets that against EPA's own multi-million-dollar cost estimate. R28 tests the order's two-year pool rule against reported inventory (92.9M lb in 1995 vs 108.2M lb today) and against import volumes. This is the cheapest possible check for an agency to act on and it is invisible to a criterion bank that asks whether a comment 'cites data' rather than whether it recomputes the agency's own.
all_names: Audits the agency's own figures, record, or arithmetic

species.name: Surfaces an affected class or case the proposal overlooked
species.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a specific category of person, entity, or operating situation that the proposal's text does not appear to contemplate, or contemplates wrongly, and shows the consequence of that gap. 10 = a concrete class or edge case is named, its exclusion or misclassification is tied to specific proposal language, and the resulting harm or absurdity is stated. 5 = a gap is gestured at but neither the class nor the consequence is made concrete. 0 = the comment discusses only the population the notice already addresses.
species.rationale: R45 makes one point and it is a real one: the listing would convert existing lawful owners of long-domesticated birds into violators overnight, a class the proposal appears to have reasoned past. R05, for all its heat, ends on a defect nobody else would report -- the intake form's self-identification list has no entry for the person the program exists to compensate. R10 finds two more: owners who did not reside at the property continuously, and extended family whose individual losses are not separately compensable. R57 supplies the mirror case on the industry side, an operator flying under 30 hours per year against a compliance clock derived from 200-300 hours per month. Coverage gaps are the highest-value thing a comment can find and nothing about their presentation makes them look impressive.
all_names: Surfaces an affected class or case the proposal overlooked

species.name: Rebuts the agency's own stated rationale on its terms
species.instruction: Score whether the comment locates the reason the agency gave for the proposal and argues directly against that reason. 10 = the agency's stated justification is identified accurately and met head-on with a counter-argument or counter-evidence addressed to it. 5 = the agency's rationale is acknowledged but the response changes the subject to the commenter's own concerns. 0 = the rationale is never engaged; the comment states a position as if the proposal had no reasoning behind it.
species.rationale: R51 does the hardest version of this: MSHA framed the revision as statutory alignment under the Appointments Clause and the APA, and USW answers that framing directly -- District Managers exercise a delegated administrative function, not significant regulatory power -- before returning to hazard evidence. R25 contests the Service's reading of its own Species Status Assessment and argues the data support endangered rather than threatened, i.e. it attacks the determination's basis, not just its conclusion. R17 explains why the agency's guidance-versus-rulemaking choice matters in a way the agency would not know: Kentucky law (KRS 13A.130) bars the Cabinet from regulating by guidance document, so uncodified guidance is inoperable for the implementing state. Answering the rationale is what makes a comment usable in the response-to-comments; restating a preference is not.
all_names: Rebuts the agency's own stated rationale on its terms

species.name: Applies a controlling standard to the facts rather than citing it
species.instruction: Score whether the comment takes a governing legal, scientific, or professional standard and works the proposal's facts through it. 10 = the standard is named, its elements are identified, and the proposal's facts are matched against those elements to show fit or misfit, with the mismatch driving the recommendation. 5 = a standard is invoked and the conclusion asserted, with the application left implicit. 0 = authority or the notice is quoted or summarized at length in place of analysis, or no standard is engaged.
species.rationale: R43 is a clean instance: the writer states the IUCN Reintroduction Guidelines constraint (do not reintroduce until the original cause of extirpation is addressed), applies it to Guam's brown tree snakes, then applies the conservation-introduction provision to the Palmyra site assessment and to the release and post-release monitoring elements one by one. R25 does the same with the statutory threatened-versus-endangered line and the resiliency/redundancy/representation framework. The contrasting failure mode is visible in R12 and R26, which reproduce large stretches of the Federal Register narrative and the procedural history and then stop short of applying anything to them -- a shape that reads as rigorous and analyzes little.
all_names: Applies a controlling standard to the facts rather than citing it

species.name: Credible alternative meeting the regulatory objective
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment proposes a specific alternative, exception, phase-in, or substitute and explains why it can achieve the same objective with relevant tradeoffs; score 0 when it only supports or opposes the proposal.
species.rationale: R09 proposes inspections and life limits, R46 proposes bag limits, and R57 argues for an alternative training-equivalence period.
all_names: Supplies a workable alternative, not just opposition or support
Credible alternative meeting the regulatory objective

species.name: Ask serves more than the commenter's own burden or exposure
species.instruction: Score the beneficiary of the requested change as the comment itself frames it. 10 = the change would improve the rule's functioning for third parties, the protected resource, or the public, including where it plainly costs the commenter something. 5 = mixed: the ask helps the commenter but the stated reasons are about workability for everyone. 0 = the entire ask is relief for the submitter -- delay, exemption, a higher threshold, more time -- with the public-interest framing supplying no independent content.
species.rationale: R25 asks the Service to list the species in a MORE restrictive category than proposed and to add incidental-take prohibitions, which is an ask against the grain of what a petitioner would want if it were optimizing for itself. R51 argues for retaining an authority exercised over its own members' employers. R56 asks for a change that would reduce, not increase, what he may keep. Against those: R34's entire content is a request for 15 additional days; R02 asks that the reporting requirement be repealed or deferred to 2023 because it is expensive for the commenter's members; R29 asks that the threshold be raised tenfold so its own office files fewer forms. All three are courteous, correctly addressed, provision-anchored, and ask the agency for nothing but their own relief -- exactly the profile a criterion bank rewards.
all_names: Ask serves more than the commenter's own burden or exposure

species.name: Requested change is material, not a single-filer scope cleanup
species.instruction: Score how much would change if the agency granted the request. 10 = adoption would alter who is covered, protected, or burdened, or by how much -- the substantive reach or stringency of the rule moves. 5 = adoption would change how the rule operates for a definable group without changing its reach. 0 = the request is an editorial, applicability, or cross-reference correction whose consequences run essentially to the filer alone, however precisely stated.
species.rationale: R35 is precise, correct-looking, and cites exact model numbers -- and asks only that three engine designations be struck from an applicability list. R39 asks whether exactly 0.125 inch is acceptable, reconciling AD text against a service bulletin. Both are the kind of narrowly scoped, perfectly formatted request that scores well on any 'specific and actionable' criterion while barely moving the rule. Set against R30 (relisting of celery powder, excluded methods, synthetic methionine -- each of which changes what may be sold as organic), R27 (which forum prosecutes drug and DUI offenses on federal land, and whether enhancements and interlock survive), and R25 (which listing category applies). Materiality and actionability are different axes and a bank that scores only the second inverts them.
all_names: Requested change is material, not a single-filer scope cleanup

species.name: Original analysis dominates reproduction of material already in the record
species.instruction: Score the proportion of the comment's substance that is the commenter's own reasoning about the proposal, as against material the agency already possesses -- block quotation or paraphrase of the notice, recitation of procedural history, and description of the commenter's own organization. Judge analytic content, not layout or length. 10 = essentially all substance is the commenter's own analysis; recited material appears only where a specific passage is being attacked. 5 = roughly half is reproduced material that carries the reader to the analysis. 0 = the comment is largely a summary of what the agency proposed plus a description of who the commenter is, with a position stated at the end.
species.rationale: R12 reproduces a long passage of the Federal Register narrative and much of its own procedural framing before reaching its questions; R26 spends its length on stakeholder rosters, the geology background, and the history of its own prior comment letters. R16 and R50 both open with extended self-description (member counts, market share, program names) before the analysis begins. None of that is information the agency lacks. Compare R18 and R56, which start inside the problem and stay there, and R10, which is nothing but its own analysis, section by section. The reproduced material makes a comment look thorough while contributing nothing to the record.
all_names: Original analysis dominates reproduction of material already in the record

species.name: Contributes site-, region-, or population-specific facts
species.instruction: Score whether the comment supplies concrete facts tied to a named place, population, or operation, of a kind the agency is unlikely to already hold. 10 = specific local facts (named programs and their funding, counts and magnitudes for a defined population, named local ecological conditions, named local operating constraints) that materially bear on the proposal. 5 = a locality is named but the facts offered about it are generic. 0 = only national or generic claims. Score the facts, not the commenter's identity or standing.
species.rationale: R15 hands NHTSA the actual channel map for its own survey question: PSAs under station licensing, personal-injury advertising, FDOT's Ridesmart and CUTR grants, and the $2.50 motorcycle registration fee against 638,883 registered motorcycles with the FRTP dismantled and residual funds flowing to a general fund. That is information a national survey design cannot generate for itself. R11 gives CMS the operating scale behind its position -- 4,084 square miles, four acute hospitals including two Level One trauma centers, roughly 600,000 unique patients a year regardless of ability to pay. R31 supplies Big Island-only breeding, native-tree nest dependence, strawberry guava invasion, and ROD dieback. R28 supplies Michigan storage tonnage. Local facts are the scarce input in rulemaking and they arrive in unimpressive packaging.
all_names: Contributes site-, region-, or population-specific facts

species.name: Names a specific administrability defect from the complier's seat
species.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a concrete, mechanism-level reason the rule will fail or misfire in execution, tied to the provision that causes it. 10 = a specific execution defect is named -- a required field or category that does not exist, a licensing or supply constraint that makes compliance impossible on the stated timeline, a cost of participating that the rule declines to recognize -- and located in the text that creates it. 5 = a real implementation difficulty is described in general terms. 0 = burden is asserted without mechanism, or the comment never reaches implementation.
species.rationale: R46 identifies something only a vendor would know: the measures depend on standardized instruments, and copyright restrictions block vendors from supplying the content and managing its cost, so a measure can be adopted and still be unimplementable. R33 names the binding constraint on a 180-day compliance window -- the small pool of physicians certified to issue second-class medicals, plus DPE examiner capacity. R05, beneath the anger, reports that the claim intake path itself is the obstacle and that its self-identification list omits the claimant category. R10 notes that claim-preparation time and appraisal and expert costs are excluded from recoverable damages, which shapes who can actually use the program. Contrast R02, which asserts burden at length and then asks for repeal rather than naming a fixable defect.
all_names: Names a specific administrability defect from the complier's seat

species.name: Transmits aggregated practitioner knowledge, not membership claims
species.instruction: Score whether a collective is functioning as a source of evidence or as a claim to authority. 10 = the comment conveys what a body of practitioners collectively knows or actually does -- documented field practice, accumulated records, joint procedures already in operation -- so the collective's experience enters the record as testable content. 5 = a collective position is asserted with one or two concrete illustrations. 0 = the organization's size, market share, or membership is offered as the reason to credit the comment, with no collective knowledge transmitted. Score transmitted knowledge, not who the submitter is.
species.rationale: R25 puts 120 working-group members behind a specific evidentiary claim and points to the field reports and meeting notes that back it, including from the people who authored the original conservation plan -- the group is an evidence base. R27 does the same for practice rather than science: it describes the joint arrangements already running (a state law permitting deputization of USFS rangers, a national MOU template developed with western sheriffs, established case-routing to state prosecution) and reasons from how those actually work. R36 reports 17 years of administering coverage for 35,000 retirees and volunteers the plan as a demonstration site. Against these, R16 and R50 lead with 440 distributors, 85% of capacity, 93% of revenue, and world's largest trade association -- authority claims where knowledge should be.
all_names: Transmits aggregated practitioner knowledge, not membership claims

species.name: Disagrees without imputing bad faith or conspiracy
species.instruction: Score whether disagreement is carried on the merits. 10 = the comment opposes strongly and never attributes corrupt, vindictive, or dishonest motive to the agency, its staff, or other parties; adverse characterizations, where made, are supported. 5 = one loaded rhetorical framing that does not carry the argument. 0 = the comment attributes bad motive as an argument (the rule exists to generate violations, the action is a vendetta by a cartel), attacks individuals, or leans on insinuation in place of evidence.
species.rationale: R21 is written by a genuinely qualified party -- A&P/IA, commercial and instrument rated, an aeronautical engineering and EE background, 6,000 hours -- and contains a real technical question about failure rates across TSO-C91 and C91a units, but it routes that through a claimed vendetta by the '406 ELT mafia' and an aside about firing a mechanic for incompetency, which converts checkable points into an accusation the agency cannot act on. R13 opens by asking whether the monitoring proposal exists to write more violations and closes on 'big brother', burying its one genuinely useful observation (charter vessels with substantial rockfish take are not required to carry VMS). R44 and R53 are grievance throughout. Formal cues -- credentials, structure, a clear ask -- survive intact in all four, so a bank keyed to those cues cannot discount them.
all_names: Disagrees without imputing bad faith or conspiracy

species.name: Marks the limits of its evidence and reasons from them
species.instruction: Score whether the comment distinguishes what it knows from what it does not, and whether the recommendation follows from that distinction. 10 = the comment states where the evidence runs out, identifies the specific unknowns, and derives a recommendation that is responsive to the uncertainty (precaution, a specified disclosure, a question the agency must answer before proceeding). 5 = uncertainty is acknowledged in passing and does not affect the recommendation. 0 = uniform certainty regardless of basis, or hedging with no consequence attached.
species.rationale: R25 turns the gap into the argument: it flags assumptions the Service made despite missing information and reasons that a lack of information argues for the more conservative classification, so the uncertainty determines the ask rather than weakening it. R60 does the methodological version -- it does not assert the study is flawed, it names precisely what is undetermined (whether results will be published and in what form, whether IRB approval or exemption is sought, how sample representativeness will be ensured, whether stratification is planned) and ties each unknown to whether the instrument can support its conclusions, including the point that the preference questions cannot be evaluated without seeing the stimulus. Against these, R44 dismisses an entire data collection as not relevant and a waste, and R23 and R48 state certainty proportional to feeling rather than evidence.
all_names: Marks the limits of its evidence and reasons from them

species.name: Provision-level defect detection
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies an exact provision, figure, definition, or version conflict and proposes a precise correction; score 0 when it offers only a generic reaction with no identifiable textual defect.
species.rationale: R06, R28, and R41 show technically specific discrepancies that broad scorecards may miss.

species.name: Quantified supporting evidence
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses relevant numerical data, calculations, comparisons, or rates to support its position; score 0 when it provides no verifiable quantitative support.
species.rationale: R30 calculates expenditures, reserves, and the proposed assessment rate, while R11 compares inventories, imports, and historical storage levels.
all_names: Quantified reasoning tied to the rule

species.name: Evidence fit and source quality
species.instruction: Score 10 when empirical, scientific, or field evidence is relevant, identifiable, appropriately current, and directly applied to the claim; score 0 when the comment relies on generic citations, credentials, or unsupported anecdotes.
species.rationale: R23 connects watershed experience to selenium criteria, R44 uses species-specific conservation evidence, and R50 supplies relevant maintenance experience.

species.name: Implementation realism
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment maps the practical steps, resources, timing, personnel, or supply-chain conditions needed to implement the proposal; score 0 when it ignores implementation realities.
species.rationale: R26 identifies repair-station scarcity, utilization, logistics, and contractual effects; R49 details design, certification, testing, manufacturing, installation, training, and supply-chain steps.

species.name: Cross-rule and system interaction
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies overlap, contradiction, gap, or sequencing with another rule, program, document, or process and specifies how to resolve it; score 0 when it analyzes the proposal in isolation.
species.rationale: R28 and R41 identify conflicts between related airworthiness directives, while R47 addresses interactions among certification procedures and permits.

species.name: Differentiated treatment
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment shows why impacts or appropriate requirements differ across relevant sizes, uses, locations, technologies, risk levels, or populations and proposes corresponding distinctions; score 0 when it assumes one uniform treatment fits all.
species.rationale: R22 distinguishes balloon operations by passenger capacity and use, while R26 distinguishes high-utilization engines from an exceptionally low-utilization aircraft.

species.name: Monitoring and adaptation design
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment specifies measurable monitoring, reporting, review triggers, corrective actions, or adaptive revisions that would reveal and address problems; score 0 when it offers no mechanism for learning or correction.
species.rationale: R12 proposes audit reporting, stricter consequences, and agency attendance during initial audits; R44 defends site-specific training changes based on inspections and accident data.

species.name: Scope and applicability precision
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment carefully identifies which entities, models, activities, geographic areas, or conditions should be covered or excluded and supports those boundaries; score 0 when its requested scope is vague or overbroad.
species.rationale: R41 specifies the affected engine models and removes unsupported models, while R55 asks targeted questions about inspection lines, government inspectors, workloads, and sampling in Poland.

species.name: Tradeoff and side-effect analysis
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment weighs the proposal’s benefits against costs, risks, displaced protections, or unintended effects and explains the relevant tradeoff; score 0 when it presents only one-sided approval or opposition.
species.rationale: R33 compares added compliance costs with claimed environmental benefit, while R22 addresses effects on pilots, doctors, training schools, insurers, and FAA administration.

species.name: Concrete administrative burden
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces burden to specific systems, forms, staffing, training, data, or recurring tasks and connects those burdens to a workable modification; score 0 when it uses only generic claims that compliance is burdensome.
species.rationale: R38 itemizes system development, data fields, testing, maintenance, and employee training, while R19 proposes specific alternatives for certification materials and timing.

species.name: Distributional consequence analysis
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies which vulnerable, dependent, underserved, or differently situated groups bear distinct effects and explains the mechanism; score 0 when it invokes broad public interest without identifying affected groups.
species.rationale: R05 connects payment policy to safety-net hospitals and hundreds of thousands of patients, while R39 explains how formulary exclusions may affect patients who respond differently to medicines.

species.name: Proposal-specific engagement
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment addresses the actual proposal’s provisions, acknowledges relevant competing considerations, and makes prioritized actionable recommendations; score 0 when it is generic support, opposition, or emotional reaction untethered to the proposal.
species.rationale: R14 identifies a specific omission and proposes amendments across reporting, training, databases, and related policies, while R17 focuses on one concrete ambiguity instead of merely endorsing or opposing the AD.

species.name: Operational burden grounded in workflow
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment describes concrete staffing, system, supply-chain, time, or cost burdens and their scale; score 0 when it merely labels a proposal costly, confusing, or burdensome.
species.rationale: R09 identifies the scarcity of qualified repair stations, R37 enumerates certification and installation work, and R43 describes reporting-system and training requirements.

species.name: Measurement validity and data integrity
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment evaluates sampling, representativeness, incentives, privacy, bias, missingness, or instrument validity and links those issues to data usefulness; score 0 when it assumes that collected data will automatically be reliable.
species.rationale: R08 questions youth-survey honesty and consent, R36 addresses sample representativeness and survey design, and R23 discusses tissue-based versus water-column measures.

species.name: Legal authority and procedural safeguards
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies governing legal authority and applies it to specific proposed language, delegation, reporting, enforcement, or safeguards; score 0 when it invokes legality or rights only in general terms.
species.rationale: R07 examines equivalency and inspection authority, R21 identifies statutory reporting requirements, and R58 applies statutory data provisions to audit safeguards.
